draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Mobor! This is the far end of the Sal river, which drains into the Arabian Sea near Betul, a coastal village known for its beach, lighthouse and fort.
draft.hungryLine: Next door at Cutbona sits South Goa's largest fishing hub, so fresh fish is the thing to look for around here.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Holy Cross Chapel at Baradi is about a 17 min walk, and Betul with its beach, lighthouse and fort is close by.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head over to Betul's beach and sit where the Sal river meets the sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Cutbona fishing jetty, right by Betul, has over 300 trawlers working out of it.

legends.title: The Miraculous Cross
legends.body: Up on the hill at Baradi stands what locals call the Miraculous Cross. Its feast is celebrated every year on 3 May.

tips.title: Plan around 3 May.
tips.body: That's the yearly feast of the Baradi Holy Cross on the hill nearby.

tips.title: Call it the Sal.
tips.body: The river here is the Sal, though people sometimes wrongly call it the Betul River because it meets the sea at Betul.

story.title: Where the river ends
story.body: The Sal river winds down through South Goa and drains into the Arabian Sea near Betul, the southernmost village of Quepem.

story.title: Saying no to a port
story.body: As of November 2025, the Betul village panchayat opposed a satellite port proposed by the Mormugao Port Authority. Opponents said it would threaten fish breeding and local fishing livelihoods.

story.title: Fishing country
story.body: Cutbona jetty next to Betul is South Goa's largest fishing hub, with over 300 trawlers. Margao is about an hour north of Betul.
